The *Padumajātaka* (Ja 261), translated as *The Lotus*, belongs to the Pali Jātaka collection. According to the narrative framework recorded at Jetavana, the Buddha delivered the story concerning several monks who presented offerings of garlands beneath "Ānanda’s tree". This tree, renowned across India, had been planted by the elder Ānanda near the gate of Jetavana; the contextual backstory is cross-referenced to the *Kāliṅgabodhi-jātaka* ("Kalinga-bodhi Birth"). The canonical core opens with the verse phrase, "Cut, and cut, and cut again". In modern studies, Oskar von Hinüber indexes Ja 261 in reference to textual variants cited within the tradition [von Hinüber 1996].
